title: Mosquito treatment
subtitle: Based on Mitch's answers and the product labels, checked against NSW requirements. Updated 6 Nov 2026.
source: Mitch's answers 6 Nov 2026; LPC Tech Onboarding Pack (PPE, never list, if something goes wrong); jobbook-data/chemicals.json (Mosquito Treatment products); jobbook-data/services.json (past wordings); researched, not from Mitch: VectoBac WG label and safety data sheet (Sumitomo Chemical Australia)

sections.heading: When this job comes up
body: Mosquito treatment for a home and its garden. Mitch's service is called Mosquito Treatment. Past invoices read: "Mosquito treatment, approved residual insecticide", "Mosquito & tick treatment to accessible gardens and lawns" and "Mosquito/midge treatment".
Treat in dry weather. Never treat near waterways.
Tell the customer straight up that there are no guarantees. How long a treatment lasts varies a lot.
The job process, the never list, PPE and the free service period are in the Every job guide.

sections.heading: What the law and the label require

items.text: Follow the product label
items.detail: Using a pesticide against its label is an offence. If the job needs something the label does not allow, stop and call Mitch.

items.text: Make the record the same day
items.detail: Every pesticide job needs a record: full product name, date, target pest, rate and quantity, address and area treated, who applied it, equipment, and start and finish times. It must be made within 48 hours and kept at least 3 years. Give the customer a copy if they ask.

items.text: Outdoor spraying: record the weather
items.detail: Write down wind speed and direction at the start and whenever it changes. Add temperature, humidity or rain if the label says it matters. A subfloor outside the walls counts as outdoors.

items.text: Keep it out of waterways
items.detail: Never spray near waterways, ponds, tanks or fish. Check the label for the distance.

items.text: Only do work your licence covers
items.detail: If a treatment is outside your licence class, work under Mitch's direct supervision and do not do it alone.

items.text: Protect people, pets and the environment
items.detail: Wear the PPE the label and SDS call for. Keep spray and bait away from people, pets, food, drains and waterways. Harming people, wildlife or property with a pesticide is an offence.

items.text: Ladders and heights
items.detail: Work from the ground where you can. Never stand on the top two steps. Keep three points of contact. All four feet down. Tie extension ladders off top and bottom.

sections.heading: What to avoid
sections.title: Mitch: 100% very important
sections.body: Never treat near waterways. Also keep clear of:
items: Ponds
Water tanks
Fish
Edible gardens
Flowering plants

sections.heading: PPE
sections.title: PPE on before you go in
sections.note: Never apply chemicals without PPE. If the SDS requires it, you wear it. No exceptions.
items: Gloves and closed shoes at minimum
Gloves, mask and eye protection for any spray, as per the product SDS

sections.heading: Products Mitch uses
sections.title: Names as in Mitch's product list. No rates here: follow the label.
rows: Country Bifenthrin 100 Low Odour Termiticide & Insecticide
Mitch's mosquito spray: all external areas and the surrounding foliage. The usual spray pump, or the new backpack sprayer.
Aquastar 100SC is the other bifenthrin Mitch has. Use whichever he has loaded, after checking its label covers mosquitoes and the area.
A larvicide for mosquito larvae in water. See the VectoBac box below.

sections.heading: What VectoBac is for
sections.title: From the label.
items: It is a biological larvicide. The label says it is for mosquito larvae only, from the first stage to the early fourth stage.
The label's uses are standing water: ponds, ditches, flood and irrigation water, tidal and stormwater areas, and small containers under 50 litres.
Do not apply it to clean, finished drinking water.
The label says do not contaminate streams, rivers or waterways with it, apart from the labelled uses.

Mitch's list shows a mister or fogger as its equipment. The label talks about ground spray gear such as a hand pump or mist blower. Use VectoBac only where its label allows (standing water and containers). Bifenthrin never goes near waterways, ponds or tanks.

sections.heading: Steps
sections.title: Steps

items.text: Check the weather first. Dry weather only
items.detail: Spray in dry weather and within the wind limits on the product label. Rebook if it is wet. Record wind speed and direction on the job.

items: Ask the customer to point out where the mosquitoes are worst

items.text: Look for where they are coming from
items.detail: Usually a waterway. Never treat near waterways. Tell the customer what you found.

items: Take BEFORE photos of the areas

items.text: Treat all the external areas and the surrounding foliage with the low odour bifenthrin
items.detail: Country Bifenthrin 100 Low Odour. Go high. Spray pump as usual, or the backpack sprayer.

items.text: Stay clear of everything in the avoid box
items.detail: Waterways, ponds, water tanks, fish, edible gardens and flowering plants.

items.text: Apply per the product label. Never exceed label rates
items.detail: Never mix chemicals without checking the label first. If in doubt, call Mitch.

items: Keep chemicals away from food, children and pets
Note anything you could not treat or reach, and why
Take AFTER photos

items.text: Record the weather on the service report
items.detail: Wind speed, wind direction and other weather on the day.

items.text: Tell the customer to keep off the treated areas as the product label says

sections.heading: Job complete when
items: BEFORE and AFTER photos taken
External areas and surrounding foliage treated, and nothing on the avoid list treated
Anything you could not treat or reach is noted on the job report, with the reason
Product, rate, area and quantity recorded on the job report
Weather on the day (wind speed, wind direction and other weather) recorded on the service report
Customer told what you did, and that there are no guarantees
Customer told how long to keep off the treated areas, as the product label says
Mosquito Treatment Information sheet given only if the customer asks for it; ask Mitch for the sheet
Service report left, or customer told it is being emailed

items.q: Will it get rid of all the mosquitoes? I'm still seeing mozzies.
items.a: There are no guarantees with mosquitoes. How long a treatment lasts varies a lot.

items.q: Have you got anything in writing about the treatment?
items.a: We can send you our Mosquito Treatment Information sheet if you'd like it.

sections.heading: Tell Mitch straight away if
sections.body: Call Mitch on 0432 181 689. After hours or urgent, call Mitch directly.

items.text: You apply the wrong chemical
items.detail: Stop immediately. Do not continue. Call Mitch.

items.text: There is a spill
items.detail: Follow the SDS procedure. Call Mitch immediately. Never leave a spill unattended.

items.text: Someone is hurt
items.detail: Treat the injury first. Call Mitch. Write down what happened.

items.text: The customer complains or gets aggressive
items.detail: Stay calm and do not argue. For a complaint, tell them Mitch will call them today. If they are aggressive, remove yourself. Call Mitch either way.

items.text: The customer asks for a quote on anything complex, or you are not sure
items.detail: Say "I'll need to get Mitch to come and have a look and provide a quote for that."

items.text: You see signs of termites or other pests outside this job
items.detail: Photograph it and tell Mitch. Termite quotes always go to Mitch.
